title: One Tube, Two Sperm, Two Fusions

scenes.tts: Shake a ripe maize tassel and a yellow haze drifts off. Each grain is a tiny plant of three cells. If it lands on a silk, it grows a tube and delivers two sperm. Both sperm normally fertilize something. Why two?
scenes.visual: Tassel and ear with silk; pollen dots drift to the silk; one grain enlarges to show a tube cell and two sperm; the tube grows and two arrows lead to two question boxes.
scenes.narration: Shake a ripe maize tassel and a yellow haze drifts off. Each grain is a tiny plant of three cells. If it lands on a silk, it grows a tube and delivers two sperm. Both sperm normally fertilize something. Why two?

scenes.tts: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to a stigma. Fertilization is the fusion of a sperm with a female cell inside the ovule. They are separate events. The grain grows a pollen tube down through the style into the ovary. The sperm have no flagella, so they ride inside the tube. Near the ovule, the tube follows chemical signals from the synergids. It bursts into one synergid and releases both sperm.
scenes.visual: Schematic stigma, style, ovary and ovule; a grain lands and a tube grows with two sperm inside; the ovule enlarges to show egg, synergids and central cell; the tube bursts into a synergid and releases two sperm.
scenes.narration: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to a stigma. Fertilization is the fusion of a sperm with a female cell inside the ovule. They are separate events. The grain grows a pollen tube down through the style into the ovary. The sperm have no flagella, so they ride inside the tube. Near the ovule, the tube follows chemical signals from the synergids. It bursts into one synergid and releases both sperm.

scenes.tts: Now count chromosomes in maize, which has twenty in its body cells. The egg carries ten. Each sperm carries ten. The central cell is a large cell of the embryo sac, with two polar nuclei. Ten plus ten makes twenty.
scenes.visual: The ovule shifts left; the egg, both sperm and both polar nuclei get a ten; the central cell gets a twenty.
scenes.caption: Now count chromosomes in maize, which has 20 in its body cells. The egg carries 10. Each sperm carries 10. The central cell is a large cell of the embryo sac, with two polar nuclei. 10 + 10 makes 20.
scenes.narration: Now count chromosomes in maize, which has 20 in its body cells. The egg carries 10. Each sperm carries 10. The central cell is a large cell of the embryo sac, with two polar nuclei. 10 + 10 makes 20.

scenes.tts: One sperm fuses with the egg. Ten plus ten makes twenty. That zygote grows into the embryo. The other sperm fuses with the central cell. Twenty plus ten makes thirty. This is the first cell of the endosperm, a tissue that stores food for the embryo.
scenes.visual: One sperm joins the egg, which becomes the green zygote; the other joins the central cell, which turns yellow; sums appear beside each.
scenes.caption: One sperm fuses with the egg. 10 + 10 makes 20. That zygote grows into the embryo. The other sperm fuses with the central cell. 20 + 10 makes 30. This is the first cell of the endosperm, a tissue that stores food for the embryo.
scenes.narration: One sperm fuses with the egg. 10 + 10 makes 20. That zygote grows into the embryo. The other sperm fuses with the central cell. 20 + 10 makes 30. This is the first cell of the endosperm, a tissue that stores food for the embryo.

scenes.tts: Now count the sets of ten. The embryo has one maternal set and one paternal set. The endosperm has two maternal sets and one paternal set. The seed coat grows from the integuments, which are the mother's own tissue. It carries twenty.
scenes.visual: Blocks of ten build the embryo (orange plus blue) and the endosperm (two orange plus blue); the integuments turn orange and a seed coat row appears.
scenes.caption: Now count the sets of 10. The embryo has one maternal set and one paternal set. The endosperm has two maternal sets and one paternal set. The seed coat grows from the integuments, which are the mother's own tissue. It carries 20.
scenes.narration: Now count the sets of 10. The embryo has one maternal set and one paternal set. The endosperm has two maternal sets and one paternal set. The seed coat grows from the integuments, which are the mother's own tissue. It carries 20.

scenes.tts: Cross a maize plant with two white alleles with pollen from a plant with two yellow alleles. The embryo has one white allele and one yellow, and the endosperm has two white alleles and one yellow. Assuming yellow is fully dominant, the kernels are yellow. This is called xenia. Keep the rule: two maternal sets and one paternal set make the endosperm, and one of each make the embryo.
scenes.visual: Two parents; the embryo gets y and Y, the endosperm y, y and Y; a yellow kernel appears; the rule is written along the bottom.
